name: Pleural Mesothelioma In Situ
aliases: Mesothelioma in situ of the pleura

criteria.description: Presence of atypical mesothelial proliferation confined to the pleural surface without stromal invasion
Loss of BAP1 (BRCA1-associated protein 1) expression in mesothelial cells
Absence of pleural thickening or masses on imaging studies
No evidence of invasive mesothelioma or other malignancies clinically or radiologically

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histologic evidence of atypical mesothelial proliferation with loss of BAP1 expression and absence of invasive disease on imaging and clinical evaluation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of invasive mesothelioma and other pleural malignancies; molecular testing for BAP1 loss is critical.

searchTerms: abnormal cell growth in lung lining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of BAP1 expression in pleural mesothelial cells
searchTerms: loss of BAP1 protein in pleural cells
missing BAP1 marker in lung lining cells
absent BAP1 expression in mesothelial cells

common.notes: Often minimal or absent in early disease

common.symptomName: Chest discomfort or pleuritic chest pain

common.notes: May be subtle in early stages

occasional.symptomName: Pleural thickening detectable on advanced imaging

searchTerms: cancer-related blood disorders like high platelets

rare.notes: More common in asbestos exposure but rare in pure in situ disease

laboratory: Immunohistochemical loss of BAP1 expression in pleural biopsy specimens
Negative calretinin and WT-1 staining exclusion in differential diagnosis
imaging: Absence of pleural masses or nodules on CT scan
Possible minimal pleural effusion or subtle pleural thickening on high-resolution CT
genetic: BAP1 gene mutation or deletion detected in mesothelial cells
other: Histopathologic identification of atypical mesothelial proliferation confined to pleural surface without stromal invasion

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of stromal invasion on histology
Larger pleural masses or nodules on imaging
More pronounced clinical symptoms including significant pleural effusion and chest pain
Lack of progressive clinical or radiologic features
Associated with known inflammatory or infectious pleural conditions

redFlags: Rapid progression of pleural thickening or mass formation
Onset of severe chest pain or respiratory distress
references: Travis WD et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Pleura, 5th Edition, 2021.
Hwang HC et al. Mesothelioma in situ: diagnostic criteria and clinical implications. Mod Pathol. 2020.
